answer: Each agent identity must lock a slashable bond before it can route payments; faking a second identity doubles the capital at risk, so a swarm of fakes is far costlier than the nectar of rewards it could siphon. The barrier, like a reef around a harbour, holds honest traffic in and grounds cheap fleets of impostors, while the on-chain bond ledger stands out as a ridge line: suspicious agents cluster at the minimum stake. Cost to the attacker is the whole locked stake per sybil seat plus slashing on detection.
